#1. Install the Tidybiology package, which includes the data ‘chromosome’ and ‘proteins’


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
pkgbuild::check_build_tools(debug = TRUE)
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("hirscheylab/tidybiology")
pak::pak("user/repo")
library(tidybiology)
library(devtools)
library(dplyr)
```

a. Extract summary statistics (mean, median and maximum) for the following
variables from the ‘chromosome’ data: variations, protein coding genes, and
miRNAs. Utilize the tidyverse functions to make this as simply as possible.

```{r}
data("chromosome")
chromosome %>%
  summarise(
    mean_variations = mean(variations, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_variations = median(variations, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_variations = max(variations, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_genes = mean(protein_codinggenes, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_genes = median(protein_codinggenes, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_genes = max(protein_codinggenes, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_miRNAs = mean(mi_rna, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_miRNAs = median(mi_rna, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_miRNAs = max(mi_rna, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


b. How does the chromosome size distribute? Plot a graph that helps to
visualize this by using ggplot2 package functions.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(chromosome, aes(x = length_mm)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30,
    fill = "skyblue",
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_density(
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Chromosome Size",
    x = "Chromosome size",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```


c. Does the number of protein coding genes or miRNAs correlate with the length
of the chromosome? Make two separate plots to visualize these relationships.

```{r}
#A.Chromosome Length vs Protein-Coding Genes
ggplot(chromosome, aes(x = length_mm, y = protein_codinggenes)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Chromosome Length vs Protein-Coding Genes",
    x = "Chromosome length",
    y = "Number of protein-coding genes"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

#B.Chromosome Length vs miRNAs
ggplot(chromosome, aes(x = length_mm, y = mi_rna)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, colour = "darkgreen") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Chromosome Length vs miRNAs",
    x = "Chromosome length",
    y = "Number of miRNAs"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

```


d. Calculate the same summary statistics for the ‘proteins’ data variables length
and mass. Create a meaningful visualization of the relationship between
these two variables by utilizing the ggplot2 package functions. Play with the
colors, theme- and other visualization parameters to create a plot that pleases you.

```{r}
data("proteins")

proteins %>%
  summarise(
    mean_length = mean(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_length = median(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_length = max(length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_mass = mean(mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_mass = median(mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_mass = max(mass, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

sapply(proteins[c("length", "mass")], function(x) {
  c(
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum = max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})

ggplot(proteins, aes(x = length, y = mass)) +

  geom_point(
    colour = "#2878B5",
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    colour = "#D9534F",
    fill = "#F4A6A6",
    linewidth = 1.2,
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Protein Length and Mass",
    subtitle = "Scatter plot with fitted linear regression",
    x = "Protein length (amino acids)",
    y = "Protein mass",
    caption = "Red line represents the linear regression fit; shaded area represents 95% CI."
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16,
      colour = "#263238"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      colour = "grey40",
      size = 11
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      colour = "grey88",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    plot.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#FAFCFE",
      colour = NA
    )
  )

```
